verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents Runbooks as its condition-based automation engine. Runbooks evaluate their conditions when an incident is declared, and steps can carry conditions tied to incident events, such as posting to Slack when a new AI summary is generated. Their actions include creating Slack channels, starting Zoom meetings and sending webhooks. Missing for 10: no evidence of automated reminders, no evidence of automated incident field changes, triggers beyond declaration and summary generation are thin, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, a condition-based workflow engine automates the toil — updates, reminders, field changes — triggered by incident events

citations.quote: Runbooks are FireHydrant's automation engine. They define and automate a workflow of steps and actions according to specified conditions.
Any time an incident is declared, Runbooks evaluate their conditions to decide whether or not they should trigger.
We'll use our runbook to then add a step with conditions for posting into Slack when a new summary has become available.
Some examples of actions include creating a Slack channel, starting a Zoom meeting
